hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok led Jeok Cheongang and me to a pavilion deep in the Inner Court, telling us to let him know if anything was uncomfortable or if we needed anything.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok led Jeok Cheongang and me to a pavilion deep in the Inner Court and told us to let him know if we needed anything or found anything uncomfortable.

hunks.baseline: At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet call, Tang Sadok—still not fully recovered—froze like a statue as he hurried to leave the pavilion.
hunks.sol: At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet call, Tang Sadok froze like a statue. Though he still hadn’t recovered, he’d been hurrying to leave the pavilion.

hunks.baseline: He slowly turned around and struggled to squeeze out a voice that wouldn’t come.
hunks.sol: He slowly turned and struggled to force out a voice.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s gaze was deep and still. After staring at Tang Sadok in silence, he suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang stared at him in silence, his gaze deep and still. Then he spoke.

hunks.baseline: Myriad-Poison Asura, my ass. The man standing before him was Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.
hunks.sol: Myriad-Poison Asura, my ass. The man standing before Tang Sadok was Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.

hunks.baseline: The current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, a venerable sect of complete thugs that popped up every now and then to turn Murim upside down whenever people least expected it.
hunks.sol: The current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan—a long-established sect of utter thugs who popped up just when people had nearly forgotten them and turned Murim upside down.

hunks.baseline: The sect had been setting fires all over the world for more than three hundred years, generation after generation. Yet when his own residence caught fire, Jeok Cheongang had wiped out more than a thousand Demonic Cult members. The very embodiment of hypocrisy.
hunks.sol: For over three hundred years, the sect had gone around setting fires across the land. Yet when his own residence caught fire, Jeok Cheongang had wiped out more than a thousand Demonic Cult members. He was hypocrisy incarnate.

hunks.baseline: A bead of cold sweat he hadn’t even noticed forming rolled down Tang Sadok’s neck. He swallowed hard and answered.
hunks.sol: A bead of cold sweat rolled down Tang Sadok’s neck. He swallowed hard.

hunks.baseline: “Let’s be careful, okay? Read the room.”
hunks.sol: “Be careful, all right? Read the room.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang gently massaged Tang Sadok’s neck as he whispered. I’d thought he looked strangely familiar, and now I knew why. He was exactly like the high school bullies who used to hang around the alleys near my elementary school.
hunks.sol: As Jeok Cheongang whispered, he gently massaged Tang Sadok’s neck. Something about the sight was oddly familiar. Then I remembered the high school bullies who used to hang around the alleys when I was in elementary school. They’d acted exactly like that.

hunks.baseline: The only problem was that those bullies had been around seventeen, while Jeok Cheongang was at least a hundred and seventeen.
hunks.sol: The problem was, those bullies had been about seventeen. Jeok Cheongang was at least a hundred and seventeen.

hunks.baseline: *How does someone rejuvenate a hundred years?*
hunks.sol: *Did he just knock a hundred years off his age?*

hunks.baseline: The low voice. The half-lidded eyes. And on top of that, a masterful choice of words for the situation.
hunks.sol: The low voice. The half-lidded eyes. Even his choice of words was perfect for the situation.

hunks.baseline: “This old man’s been in a bit of a bad mood lately. So, how do you think I’d feel if a certain kind of story got around Murim right now?”
hunks.sol: “This old man’s been in a bit of a bad mood lately. Now, suppose a certain kind of story starts making the rounds in Murim. How do you think I’d feel?”

hunks.baseline: “Not just displeased. It’d ruin my whole day. I’d completely lose it.”
hunks.sol: “Not just displeased. It’d ruin my whole day. I’d lose my damn mind.”

hunks.baseline: “Your late father, the Poison King, and I had a decent history together. We weren’t close enough to call each other best friends, but he was someone I could trust with my back.”
hunks.sol: “Your late father, the Poison King, and I knew each other reasonably well. I wouldn’t say we were close friends, but he was a man I could trust to watch my back.”

hunks.baseline: The Poison King, who’d died a few months earlier at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, who was after the Myriad-Poison Ring, had been the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Grand Family Head and Tang Sadok’s father. But before that, he’d been a hero who, alongside Jeok Cheongang, had brought the Great Faction War to a victorious close as one of the Ten Kings.
hunks.sol: The Poison King had died a few months earlier at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, who had been after the Myriad-Poison Ring. He’d been the Grand Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan and Tang Sadok’s father. Before that, he’d been one of the Ten Kings, a hero who had helped bring the Great Faction War to a victorious close alongside Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: “He had a bit of a gloomy streak, but he was smart and quick on the uptake. One day, he poisoned the liquor I was about to drink. Then, when he saw that Peng Cheolhu, the Thunderbolt Saber King, was getting the hell beaten out of him, he casually knocked over my cup. Do you know what happened after that?”
hunks.sol: “He had a gloomy streak, but he was smart and quick on the uptake. One day, he poisoned the liquor I was about to drink. Then he saw the Thunderbolt Saber King getting the hell beaten out of him and casually knocked over my cup. Do you know what happened after that?”

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok answered in a hoarse voice.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok answered hoarsely.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. You said you’d let it go this once, then suddenly beat my father up three months later…”
hunks.sol: “Yes. You said you’d let it go that once, then suddenly beat my father up three months later…”

hunks.baseline: “N-no. My father wondered about it for years, right up until a few years ago.”
hunks.sol: “N-no. My father was still wondering about it until a few years ago.”

hunks.baseline: “I was in a foul mood, and there wasn’t anyone around to hit. So I hit him.”
hunks.sol: “I was in a foul mood that day, and there was no one else around to hit. So I hit him.”

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok’s jaw dropped as he learned the reason behind a beating that had remained a mystery for more than fifty years. And I instinctively opened my mouth.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok’s jaw dropped. After more than fifty years, he’d finally learned why his father had been beaten up. I opened my mouth on instinct.

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t that just being a lunatic?”
hunks.sol: “Isn’t that just a madman?”

hunks.baseline: A suffocating silence descended. Jeok Cheongang stared at me wordlessly, then slowly parted his lips.
hunks.sol: A suffocating silence fell. Jeok Cheongang stared at me without a word, then slowly parted his lips.

hunks.baseline: At Jeok Cheongang’s thunderous shout, Tang Sadok looked at me with the relieved expression of a man whose fifty-year-old indigestion had finally cleared up, then shot out of the pavilion like a streak of light.
hunks.sol: At the thunderous shout, Tang Sadok looked at me with the relieved expression of a man whose fifty-year-old indigestion had finally cleared up. Then he shot out of the pavilion like a streak of light.

hunks.baseline: *Was he a lizard?*
hunks.sol: *Is he a lizard?*

hunks.baseline: But I could hardly blame him when I’d just made a huge, beautiful mess all by myself. I took a steadying breath and spoke calmly.
hunks.sol: But I could hardly blame him when I’d just made such a huge, spectacular mess all by myself. I steadied my breathing and spoke calmly.

hunks.baseline: “Everything. From beginning to end.”
hunks.sol: “All of it. From beginning to end.”

hunks.baseline: “Our sect’s rules say anyone who spouts bullshit from beginning to end gets beaten twice as much.”
hunks.sol: “Our sect has a rule: anyone who spouts bullshit from beginning to end gets beaten twice as hard.”

hunks.baseline: “What lunatic—no, what esteemed person came up with that rule?”
hunks.sol: “What lunatic—no, who came up with that rule?”

hunks.baseline: If excuses weren’t going to work, it was time to adapt. I dropped to my knees as fast as if Hyuk Mujin had possessed me.
hunks.sol: If excuses weren’t going to work, it was time to adapt. I dropped to my knees so fast you’d think Hyuk Mujin had possessed me.

hunks.baseline: “I was called a lunatic by the brat who’s supposed to be my Disciple. I ought to go die, don’t you think?”
hunks.sol: “The brat who’s supposed to be my Disciple called me a madman. I ought to go off and die, don’t you think?”

hunks.baseline: I slowly lifted my deeply bowed head. Jeok Cheongang’s massive pectorals looked like they were at least an E-cup.
hunks.sol: I cautiously raised my bowed head. Jeok Cheongang’s massive pecs looked like they were at least an E-cup.

hunks.baseline: He’d recovered his youth and sharpness through Bone Transformation.
hunks.sol: He’d regained his youth and vigor through Bone Transformation.

hunks.baseline: At that point, rather than him going off somewhere to die, he could tell everyone except me to go die instead.
hunks.sol: Rather than going off somewhere to die, a man built like that could tell everyone except me to drop dead.

hunks.baseline: “No, Old Master. You’ll live a long life. Though you’ve already lived one.”
hunks.sol: “No, Old Master. You’ll live a long life. Though you already have.”

hunks.baseline: “I see. But from where I’m standing, you look like you’ll die young.”
hunks.sol: “I see. But you look like you’ll die young.”

hunks.baseline: “Please don’t say things like that. You’re hurting my feelings.”
hunks.sol: “Please don’t say that. It hurts my feelings.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m the one who ought to be more hurt. I shaved my perfectly good head clean and went all the way to Nanman pretending to be a monk, and you dare stab me in the back like this?”
hunks.sol: “I’m the one whose feelings are hurt. I shaved off a perfectly good head of hair and went all the way to Nanman pretending to be a monk, and you dare stab me in the back like this?”

hunks.baseline: I cautiously raised my head.
hunks.sol: I stole another glance up.

hunks.baseline: Then sunlight poured through the window and flashed off Jeok Cheongang’s forehead in a surprise Solar Fist attack. I reflexively squinted.
hunks.sol: Sunlight poured through the window, flashed off Jeok Cheongang’s head, and hit me with a surprise Solar Fist attack. I squinted on instinct.

hunks.baseline: “Someone once said, ‘The best time to start is when you think it’s too late.’”
hunks.sol: “Someone once said the best time to start is when you think it’s too late.”

hunks.baseline: “Before I do anything, I want to ask you one thing.”
hunks.sol: “Before I do anything, let me ask you one thing.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang looked down at me calmly and continued.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang looked down at me calmly.

hunks.baseline: “You said you came from the realm of immortals. You must be different in some way.”
hunks.sol: “You said you came from the realm of immortals. Surely you must be different in some way.”

hunks.baseline: “You, even in the realm of immortals?”
hunks.sol: “Even the you in the realm of immortals?”

hunks.baseline: “I’m dead. I’ve only got one coin left. That was my last life from the very beginning.”
hunks.sol: “I die there too. I’ve only got one coin. This was my one and only last life from the start.”

hunks.baseline: Come on. Why would he ask something like that?
hunks.sol: Come on. Why was he asking me that?

hunks.baseline: With my knees knocking, I sprang to my feet and bowed deeply to Jeok Cheongang. Once didn’t seem like enough, so I did it twice.
hunks.sol: My knees went weak. I sprang to my feet and bowed deeply to Jeok Cheongang. Once didn’t seem like enough, so I did it twice.

hunks.baseline: Whoom.
hunks.sol: *Whoom.*

hunks.baseline: A tremendous sound of breaking air rang out before he’d even finished speaking.
hunks.sol: Before he’d even finished speaking, the air split with a tremendous roar.

hunks.baseline: I squeezed my eyes shut on instinct and suddenly thought of Hyuk Mujin. If I made it out alive, I resolved to treat him much better than before. Then I gritted my teeth and swallowed a breath.
hunks.sol: I squeezed my eyes shut and suddenly thought of Hyuk Mujin. If I made it out alive, I’d treat him much better from now on. I gritted my teeth and held my breath.

hunks.baseline: Tap.
hunks.sol: *Tap.*

hunks.baseline: Whoosh!
hunks.sol: *Whoosh!*

hunks.baseline: Along with a faint touch against my forehead, a fierce gust of wind whipped my hair around.
hunks.sol: Something touched my forehead. A fierce rush of hot wind whipped my hair around.

hunks.baseline: As the hot wind died down, I opened my eyes in confusion and saw Jeok Cheongang pressing a finger to my forehead, sighing heavily with an irritated look on his face.
hunks.sol: As the wind died down, I opened my eyes in confusion. Jeok Cheongang had a finger pressed to my forehead and was sighing in irritation.

hunks.baseline: His eyes, however, held affection and joy at seeing me again.
hunks.sol: But his eyes held affection, and the joy of seeing me again.

hunks.baseline: “You little monster. Stop making such a fuss and get up already.”
hunks.sol: “You wretch. Stop making such a fuss and get up.”

hunks.baseline: “If you’re going to do it, do it properly. Like…bowing, for instance.”
hunks.sol: “If you’re going to do it, do it properly. For instance… Yes, bowing.”

hunks.baseline: I blinked dumbly. Jeok Cheongang glanced toward the window, where sunlight streamed in, and muttered:
hunks.sol: I blinked at him. Jeok Cheongang glanced toward the sunlit window and muttered,

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know why laughter suddenly escaped me at that moment.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know why I suddenly laughed.

hunks.baseline: No—that wasn’t true. I already knew.
hunks.sol: No. I did know.

hunks.baseline: “Nothing. Let me give you my bow. I’ll make it a proper nine-bow ritual.”
hunks.sol: “Nothing. Just accept my bows. I’ll give you a proper nine-bow ritual.”

hunks.baseline: “We never formally established a Master-Disciple bond. What’s the point of that kind of empty ritual? Just behave yourself from now on.”
hunks.sol: “We’ve never formally established a Master-Disciple bond. What’s the point of that empty ceremony? Just behave yourself from now on.”

hunks.baseline: He was right. Jeok Cheongang and I had never formally established a Master-Disciple bond.
hunks.sol: He was right. Jeok Cheongang and I had never formally become Master and Disciple.

hunks.baseline: An old man who had come out into the world to eliminate the Disciple who had once been like family to him needed a new successor to carry on his sect’s teachings. And a young man struggling to stay alive needed greater strength.
hunks.sol: An old man had come back into the world to eliminate a Disciple who had once been like family to him. He needed a new successor to carry on his sect’s teachings. A young man struggling to stay alive needed greater strength.

hunks.baseline: They’d come together because each needed what the other had. And so the nine-bow ritual was nothing but meaningless ceremony.
hunks.sol: They had come together because each needed what the other had. The nine-bow ritual meant nothing to them. It was an empty ceremony.

hunks.baseline: Yes, that was definitely how it had been.
hunks.sol: Yes. That was how it had been.

hunks.baseline: *It stings a little, hearing him say that.*
hunks.sol: *It stings a little, hearing him say it.*

hunks.baseline: At some point, what had once felt natural began to sting, and what had stung began to feel natural.
hunks.sol: At some point, what I’d taken for granted had begun to hurt, and what had once hurt had become something I took for granted.

hunks.baseline: And this changed feeling wasn’t something only I was allowed to have.
hunks.sol: And I wasn’t the only one whose feelings had changed.

hunks.baseline: A single word suddenly reached my ear.
hunks.sol: A single word reached me.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang continued, gazing at the sunlit window. His eyes seemed to be looking at something far away.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang kept his gaze on the sunlit window. His eyes seemed fixed on something far away.

hunks.baseline: His voice gradually grew faint, then scattered into the breeze.
hunks.sol: His voice faded and scattered into the breeze.

hunks.baseline: The rest of what he’d left unsaid—not with my ears, but with my heart.
hunks.sol: Not the rest of his words—he never finished them. I heard what he meant, not with my ears, but with my heart.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang answered without turning his head. Maybe he couldn’t bring himself to turn and face me.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang answered without turning his head. Maybe he couldn’t bring himself to face me.

hunks.baseline: “What? Why?”
hunks.sol: “Ah, what?”

hunks.baseline: His reaction was exactly what I’d expected, and it made me laugh out loud. Then I said the words I’d kept in my heart for a long time.
hunks.sol: It was exactly the reaction I’d expected, and I laughed aloud. Then I said something I’d kept in my heart for a long time.

hunks.baseline: “It’s good to see you again. To have you still here, close by.”
hunks.sol: “It’s good to see you again. And to have you still here, close by.”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, Jeok Cheongang’s shoulders, which had gone rigid, relaxed.
hunks.sol: The tension went out of Jeok Cheongang’s rigid shoulders.

hunks.baseline: He slowly turned to look at me with an expression I couldn’t quite read.
hunks.sol: He slowly turned to look at me, his expression impossible to read.

hunks.baseline: As though he’d never once had to figure out what expression to make in a moment like this, he forced his brows into a frown and twisted his lips awkwardly.
hunks.sol: As if he’d never once had to decide what face to make at a moment like this, he forced a frown and twisted his lips awkwardly.

hunks.baseline: But everyone learns from experience.
hunks.sol: But everyone learns through experience.

hunks.baseline: No matter how much a person denies it, no matter how unfamiliar it feels, they can’t hide what’s in their heart.
hunks.sol: No matter how much a person denies what they feel, no matter how unfamiliar it is, they can’t hide it forever.

hunks.baseline: That was true even of the man who had lived for more than a century with a hot, hard mask over his face—the face Murim had named the Fire King.
hunks.sol: Not even a man who had spent more than a century behind the hot, hard mask Murim had named the Fire King.

hunks.baseline: “Welcome…”
hunks.sol: “Wel…”

hunks.baseline: His voice faltered. His expression was still awkwardly tangled with feelings he hadn’t yet decided how to handle.
hunks.sol: His voice faltered. His expression was a strange tangle of feelings he still didn’t know what to do with.

hunks.baseline: But the next moment, his stubborn eyes curved into a gentle arc.
hunks.sol: Then his stubborn eyes curved gently.

hunks.baseline: A voice as warm as the sunlight reached my ear like a soft breeze.
hunks.sol: His voice reached me like a soft breeze, as warm as the sunlight.
